description: The theory and numerics of pricing financial claims: no-arbitrage and state prices, equilibrium models, forwards and swaps, options in discrete and continuous time, interest-rate and credit derivatives, and numerical methods. Students derive prices analytically, then verify and extend them with simulation, trees and finite-difference code in the lab.
modelledOn: Hull, Options, Futures and Other Derivatives
Shreve, Stochastic Calculus for Finance I and II
Glasserman, Monte Carlo Methods in Financial Engineering
outcomes: Derive prices from the no-arbitrage principle using state prices, replication and risk-neutral measures.
Explain and test equilibrium pricing models, from the CAPM to multi-factor models, against data.
Price and hedge forwards, futures, swaps and options in binomial and Black-Scholes frameworks and compute the Greeks.
Build and compare interest-rate and credit models and use them to value caps, swaptions and credit default swaps.
Implement Monte Carlo, finite-difference and Fourier pricing methods and quantify their numerical error.
Assess model risk by calibrating models to market quotes and testing hedging performance.

units.title: One-period markets and state prices
topics: Securities, payoffs and portfolios; complete and incomplete markets
No-arbitrage and the law of one price; detecting arbitrage with linear programming
State prices and the fundamental theorem of asset pricing in one period
The stochastic discount factor and the pricing kernel
Risk-neutral probabilities, replication, uniqueness and market completeness

units.title: Portfolio theory and equilibrium asset pricing
topics: Mean-variance portfolio choice, the efficient frontier and the two-fund theorem
The CAPM: derivation, the security market line and beta estimation
Expected utility, risk aversion and consumption-based pricing; the equity premium puzzle
Multi-factor models: APT, Fama-French factors and cross-sectional tests
Market efficiency and behavioural critiques; evidence from frontier markets such as the Ghana Stock Exchange

units.title: Forwards, futures, bonds and swaps
topics: Cost-of-carry forward pricing with storage costs and convenience yield; cocoa and gold forwards
Futures versus forwards: margining, marking to market, basis risk and the minimum-variance hedge ratio
Bonds and the yield curve: bootstrapping, forward rates, duration and convexity
Interest-rate and currency swaps priced as bond portfolios; hedging cedi exposure
Foreign exchange forwards and covered interest parity

units.title: Options in discrete time
topics: Option payoffs and strategies, put-call parity and no-arbitrage bounds
One-period binomial replication and risk-neutral valuation
Multi-period Cox-Ross-Rubinstein trees and American options with early exercise
Convergence of the binomial model to Black-Scholes and discrete delta hedging
Trinomial trees and implied trees

units.title: Option pricing in continuous time
topics: Brownian motion, geometric Brownian motion, the Ito integral and Ito's lemma
The Black-Scholes PDE by delta hedging and the Black-Scholes formula
Risk-neutral measure, Girsanov's theorem, Feynman-Kac and change of numeraire
The Greeks: delta, gamma, vega, theta and rho; delta-gamma hedging and hedging error
Implied volatility, the smile and skew; local volatility and the Heston stochastic volatility model
Exotic options: barrier, Asian and lookback payoffs

units.title: Interest-rate and credit derivatives
topics: Short-rate models: Vasicek, CIR and Hull-White; affine bond pricing
The HJM framework and market models; caps, floors and swaptions priced with Black's formula
Credit risk: the Merton structural model and reduced-form intensity models
Credit default swap pricing and bootstrapping hazard rates from spreads
Counterparty risk: credit valuation adjustment and collateral; pricing sovereign Eurobonds

units.title: Numerical pricing methods
topics: Monte Carlo pricing and variance reduction: antithetic and control variates; standard errors
Pathwise and likelihood-ratio Greeks; the Longstaff-Schwartz method for American options
Finite-difference schemes: explicit, implicit and Crank-Nicolson; stability and boundary conditions
Fourier methods: characteristic functions, the Carr-Madan formula and FFT pricing
Calibration and model risk: least-squares fitting to quotes and hedging performance backtests

units.title: Project and market practice
topics: Comparing pricing frameworks: when each model fails and what it assumes
Project: price and hedge a structured product, such as a cocoa-linked note with a protective floor
Critical reading of a derivatives pricing paper and its model risk discussion
Market structure and regulation: central clearing, margin rules, Basel treatment and derivative market development in Africa

schedule.title: Arbitrage and state prices
schedule.exercise: Given a three-state market with two securities and a bond, decide whether an arbitrage exists, and if not, find the set of state prices.

tasks.title: Check three small one-period markets for arbitrage by solving the payoff matrix, and exhibit an arbitrage portfolio where one exists.
Solve for the state price vector in a complete three-state market with matrix algebra and price a new payoff with it.
Write a linear program that tests for arbitrage in a market with eight assets and five states, and return the arbitrage portfolio found.

schedule.title: Discount factors and risk-neutral pricing
schedule.exercise: Show that pricing with state prices, with the stochastic discount factor and with risk-neutral probabilities give the same price, and say what changes when the market is incomplete.

tasks.title: Compute risk-neutral probabilities from state prices and a risk-free rate, and price a call payoff in a two-state market.
Find the stochastic discount factor for a market with real-world probabilities and verify it prices all traded securities exactly.
In an incomplete market with four states and two assets, compute the no-arbitrage price interval for a third payoff by optimising over state prices.

schedule.title: Portfolio choice and the CAPM
schedule.exercise: Derive the minimum-variance portfolio for two risky assets and then show the market portfolio is on the efficient frontier under CAPM assumptions.

tasks.title: Plot the efficient frontier for three stocks from given means and covariances and mark the minimum-variance portfolio.
Estimate betas for five listed Ghanaian stocks from monthly return data by regression and draw the security market line.
Optimise a portfolio under a no-short-selling constraint and compare its frontier and out-of-sample Sharpe ratio with the unconstrained solution.

schedule.title: Utility, factors and market efficiency
schedule.exercise: Read a paper on size and value factors and write a one-page critique of its method, then discuss whether the evidence should transfer to a small frontier market.

tasks.title: Compute the certainty equivalent and risk premium for a gamble under log and power utility with two risk-aversion values.
Run a Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regression on 30 stocks and 60 months of data, and report the estimated factor risk premia.
Test weak-form efficiency on daily returns of a frontier market index with autocorrelation and runs tests, and discuss the effect of thin trading.

schedule.title: Forwards, futures and bond mathematics
schedule.exercise: A cocoa exporter must sell 500 tonnes in six months. Price a forward with storage costs and design a futures hedge, stating the basis risk left.

tasks.title: Price a six-month gold forward from spot, interest rate and storage cost, and check for an arbitrage if the quoted forward is higher.
Bootstrap a zero curve from five bond prices and compute the implied forward rates and the duration of a ten-year bond.
Estimate the minimum-variance hedge ratio from spot and futures price changes, and measure hedge effectiveness before and after a basis shock.

schedule.title: Swaps and currency forwards
schedule.exercise: Value a five-year fixed-for-floating interest-rate swap from a given discount curve, then explain how a firm with cedi revenue and dollar debt would use a currency swap.

tasks.title: Compute the fixed swap rate for a three-year annual swap from a given discount factor table and the swap's value after rates rise.
Check covered interest parity for cedi and dollar rates, and construct the arbitrage when the quoted forward breaks it.
Value a cross-currency swap by discounting both legs on their own curves, and stress the value under a 15 percent cedi depreciation.

schedule.title: Binomial option pricing
schedule.exercise: Price a one-year American put on a three-step tree by hand, identify the nodes where early exercise is optimal, and compare with the European value.

tasks.title: Replicate a call on a one-period binomial stock with shares and bonds, and check the cost equals the risk-neutral price.
Build a Cox-Ross-Rubinstein tree for American and European puts and mark the nodes where early exercise is optimal.
Show that binomial prices converge to the Black-Scholes value as steps grow from 5 to 1000, and plot the oscillating error.

schedule.title: Stochastic calculus and Black-Scholes
schedule.exercise: Derive the Black-Scholes PDE by constructing a riskless hedged portfolio, then show how the formula follows from the risk-neutral expectation.

tasks.title: Simulate 20 geometric Brownian motion paths and check that the mean and variance of log returns match the theoretical values.
Implement the Black-Scholes call and put formulas and verify put-call parity across 100 random parameter sets.
Apply Ito's lemma to derive the dynamics of ln S and S squared, and confirm each with simulation to within sampling error.

schedule.title: Greeks, smiles and exotics
schedule.exercise: A trader sold 1000 calls. Compute the delta hedge, rebalance daily in a simulated path, and explain the hedging error in terms of gamma and volatility mismatch.

tasks.title: Plot delta, gamma and vega of a call against the stock price and identify where gamma is largest.
Invert Black-Scholes by root-finding to compute implied volatilities for a table of option quotes and plot the smile.
Price a down-and-out barrier call and an arithmetic Asian call by simulation, and compare each with its vanilla counterpart.

schedule.title: Short-rate and market models
schedule.exercise: Derive the Vasicek zero-coupon bond price and explain why the model can produce negative rates and how Hull-White fits today's curve.

tasks.title: Simulate Vasicek short-rate paths and verify the simulated mean reversion matches the model's long-run mean and speed.
Compute zero-coupon bond prices from the Vasicek formula and fit its parameters to a given yield curve by least squares.
Price a cap as a strip of caplets with Black's formula, and compare the result with a Monte Carlo price in a short-rate model.

schedule.title: Credit risk and counterparty risk
schedule.exercise: Use the Merton model to compute the default probability and credit spread of a firm with given assets, debt and volatility, and discuss the model's failings.

tasks.title: Compute the Merton default probability and credit spread for a firm with given asset value, debt, volatility and horizon.
Bootstrap a piecewise-constant hazard rate curve from five CDS spreads and price a new CDS at an intermediate maturity.
Estimate the credit valuation adjustment of a five-year swap by simulating exposure paths and applying the counterparty hazard rate.

schedule.title: Monte Carlo, finite differences, Fourier and calibration
schedule.exercise: Price the same European call by Monte Carlo, Crank-Nicolson finite differences and Fourier inversion, and tabulate error against computing time.

tasks.title: Price a European call by Monte Carlo with 10000 and 1000000 paths and report the standard error against the closed-form price.
Solve the Black-Scholes PDE with explicit and implicit finite differences and show the explicit scheme becoming unstable when the time step is too large.
Price an American put with the Longstaff-Schwartz regression method and compare the price and exercise boundary with the binomial tree result.

schedule.title: Model risk, structured products and regulation
schedule.exercise: Present the project: the product design, the model chosen, the price and hedge, the model risk, and a stress test of the hedge under a volatility spike.

tasks.title: Compare Black-Scholes, binomial and Heston prices for one option and tabulate the assumptions and differences in each.
Decide how an exporter's hedging programme should be cleared and margined under three regulatory scenarios, and score the choices against the case rubric.
Price a cocoa-linked note with a floor by simulation, build a delta hedge, and report hedging profit and loss across 1000 simulated price paths.
